newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SOCCER-AFRICAN CHAMPIONS LEAGUE ENTERS NEW ERA.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-AFRICAN CHAMPIONS LEAGUE ENTERS NEW ERA.

text.p: African soccer enters a fresh era at the weekend with the start of the new Champions League as 12 clubs compete in the first leg of the preliminary round of the competition.

The new league was announced last year in a bid by the Confederation of African Football (CAF) to generate badly-needed revenue for its leading club competition and has now attracted a US$3-million sponsorship and rights deal involving two French companies.
The six preliminary round matches will still be played on a knockout basis over two legs, as will the first round clashes in March and the eight second round ties in May.

But after that, following the old European Cup example of the early 1990s, the eight quarter-finalists will be divided into two groups in September and play each other on a league basis over six matches before the two group winners go through to the traditional two-legged final in December.

Few of the teams competing in this weekend's preliminary round, first leg matches will have any serious aspirations of making it through to the league competition later in the year, although a healthy entry in this year's tournament is an indication of the excitement generated by the new league.

Tanzania's Young Africans hosts neighbours Express from Uganda in potentially the biggest clash of the weekend -- both clubs having some pedigree in past competitions and being unusually forced to play in the preliminary round by the high entry level.

Clubs from Equatorial Guinea, Liberia, Malawi and the Seychelles return to the competition after varying years of non-entry but there have been late withdrawals from the Central African Republic, Namibia and Swaziland.
Preliminary round ties are also scheduled on the weekend for both the African Cup Winners' Cup and the CAF Cup, which will keep their traditional two-legged knockout format.
All the return legs will be played in two weeks' time.
